title: Streaming percentile telemetry and diff heatmap per route/model/region
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We need robust p95/p99 tracking at the granularity of route + model + region with low overhead. Current percentile reporting is batch-y and slow to diagnose regressions for production workloads (customers observe latency spikes during bursts). This ticket introduces a streaming percentile emitter (approximate quantile) that maintains rolling p95/p99 and tokens/sec counters per window, a diff/heatmap dashboard to surface recent deltas, and an automated regression detector that opens an alert channel when percentiles diverge from baseline beyond configurable thresholds. The implementation must be safe for hosted and dedicated environments (minimal CPU overhead, bounded memory), and integrate with the load-testing harness for regression playback and verification.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits approximate p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec per 1m and 5m windows grouped by (route, model, region) with <=5% additional CPU overhead under 200rps
Dashboards include a time-series panel and a diff heatmap showing delta in p95/p99 and tokens/sec across last 24h vs baseline, filterable by route/model/region
Automated regression detector alerts when p95 or p99 increases beyond absolute or relative thresholds (configurable) and includes sample request IDs and top contributing routes/models
Integration test in load harness can replay a recorded workload and detect a known regression (test artifact provided), and the detector flags the regression within the expected window
API for exporting raw percentile buckets and t-digest sketches for forensic playbacks available to SRE/REs (RBAC protected in Private deployments)
implementation_plan: Design: pick approximate streaming quantile algorithm (t-digest vs CKMS); run microbenchmarks to compare memory/CPU and merge characteristics

Runtime: implement lightweight emitter in serving runtime that increments token counters and updates quantile sketches per request grouping key (route, model, region); sampling fallback for very high QPS
Aggregation: implement rollup job that merges sketches into 1m/5m aggregates and persists to telemetry store (clickhouse/prom) with TTL
Regression Detector: implement change-point logic using both relative delta and nonparametric test (AD or Mann-Whitney) with rate-of-change smoothing; provide config flags per customer/route
Dashboards: create Grafana panels - time-series, diff heatmap, top-contributors table, and per-request sample drilldown linking to logs/trace
Load Harness: add playback scenario and golden baseline recordings; validate detector flags known regressions and does not produce false positives under synthetic noise
E2E: add CI job to run a short synthetic load test on PRs that touch telemetry / runtime code paths
Rollout: canary the emitter with 5% traffic, monitor telemetry overhead for 72h, then 25% and full rollout with rollback hooks
telemetry_schema: Emit series: telemetry.percentiles.{route}.{model}.{region}.p50/p95/p99 (numeric), telemetry.tokens_per_sec.{route}.{model}.{region} (numeric). Sketch export: sketches.percentile.{route}.{model}.{region}.tdigest (base64). Tags: route, model, region, deployment_type (hosted|dedicated|private), shard_id.
dashboards_to_create: Latency Delta Heatmap (route x model matrix) - shows percent change in p95/p99 over baseline
Per-route Percentile Timeline - p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec overlay
Regression Alerts Panel - recent detector hits with contributing routes/models and sample ids
Forensics Panel - sketch inspector + ability to compare two time windows side-by-side
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Benchmarks and choose t-digest variant (local perf 1 week)
Phase 1: Instrument runtime behind a feature flag; enable for internal staging and run emulator harness
Phase 2: Canary on 5% of traffic in hosted region us-west-2 for 72h; monitor CPU, memory, and telemetry volume
Phase 3: Increase to 25% for 48h and validate against load harness replays
Phase 4: Full rollout with automated revert if emitter causes >7% CPU increase or >2% error increase
comments: 2025-02-13 - Asha: initial spike analysis attached to design doc. Observed that p99 jumps correlate with backend cache misses — added tokens/sec overlay to correlate throughput changes.
2025-02-15 - Miguel: benchmarked t-digest and CKMS on p4d-small sample traces; t-digest had 40% smaller merge cost, chose t-digest with compression=100
2025-02-19 - Riley Chen (SRE): recommended retention of per-minute aggregates for 30 days and sketches for 7 days; added RBAC note for Private deployments
2025-02-22 - PM review (Tara Singh): asked for explicit detector tuning UI and a way to suppress known seasonal patterns per route
2025-02-24 - Miguel: implemented prototype emitter behind flag; staging load harness run shows ~3.2% CPU increase at 250rps; moving to canary next
notes: Be conservative with memory footprint for sketches on hot routes. For extremely high-throughput routes consider switching to sampled sketch updates and rely on tokens/sec for short windows.
implementation_risks: Sketch merge cost under bursty merges, increased storage from sketches, potential RBAC complexity for Private customers. Mitigations: choose high-compression t-digest, TTLs, and flag-based rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sketch correctness, benchmark suite for CPU/memory, integration tests in harness that replay known regressions, and an automated canary gate that checks telemetry pipeline health and alert false-positive rate.
